sources.citation: Pekkanen, Inka. 1981. Some consonantal sound changes in the Kadazan dialects of the Penampang, Papar, and Beaufort Districts of Sabah, Malaysia. Borneo Research Bulletin 13(1): 33-47. (Summer Institute of Linguistics, Malaysia Branch survey data.)
sources.note: Nothing on stress, accent or tone. Content for group B (Beaufort = Klias River Kadazan): word-initial t~d correspondence set; medial /z/ (not EPP /y/); /l/ where WPP/WP have /h/ (lamin 'house', likud 'back'); root-initial d/r/zero where other groups have l, r, y (dom 'leaf', roo 'chin', alan 'trail', omou 'tear', asam 'rain'); no intervocalic /r/ and no intervocalic /h/, with lengthening of the vowel when the flanking vowels are identical; no s/h metathesis; w~v~b variation (Kinamam b, Takuli v: batu/vatu 'stone', bavang 'river'); bulan 'moon', bulanut; akod 'leg'; word-final EPP /l,r/ = zero…

sources.citation: Prentice, D. J. 1970. The linguistic situation in northern Borneo. In S. A. Wurm & D. C. Laycock (eds.), Pacific linguistic studies in honour of Arthur Capell, 369-408. Pacific Linguistics C-13. Canberra: Australian National University.
sources.note: Nothing. Lexicostatistical classification of the Idahan (Dusunic/Murutic/Bisaya) languages with nomenclature, research history, maps and an annotated bibliography of sources to 1969; no phonological notes; the words stress, accent, penult(imate), tone do not occur. 'Klias' appears only as the location of Tatanaq ('Bundu', Klias Peninsula north of Klias R.) and Northern Bisaya; the Coastal Dusun 'Kadazan dialect' is given only Papar and Putatan subdialects ('Other subdialects are known to exist'), so the Klias River / Beaufort Kadazan are not distinguished.
